newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bombing victims sorry for McVeigh family.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bombing victims sorry for McVeigh family.

text.p: While most people who lost loved ones wanted Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh to die, many were still able on Friday to summon up compassion for his family.
"It's sad to get a feeling of joy when you're putting someone to death," said Dan McKinney, whose wife Linda died in the bombing.
"It was a release of the weight that has been on my shoulders for two years. It was a feeling of joy - then sadness started taking over," McKinney said.
"His parents are the ones who will be hurting. He's going to be put to sleep," said Marsha Kight, whose 23-year-old daughter Frankie Merrell was among the 168 people who died in the bombing.
After 11 hours of deliberation over two days, jurors in the McVeigh trial voted on Friday for death penalty for the 29-year-old Gulf War veteran.
"I feel sad for the McVeighs - they're going to lose a son," said Rudy Guzman whose brother Randy died in the April P. Murrah federal building in the April 19, 1995 bombing.
But Guzman said he did not regret the death sentence. "I'm satisfied. He deserved it. But it's not going to bring everyone back," Guzman said outside the courthouse.
"I got what I wanted. It's not a lot of fun to put a guy to death, but it wasn't a lot of fun when he put our loved ones to death," said Roy Sells, whose wife Lee died in the bombing.

"I wonder what Jennifer McVeigh is thinking right now," Kight said of McVeigh's younger sister who testified about her brother's anti-government sentiments and who cried in the courthouse when the death sentence was announced.
